Joint model selection for ordinary GWR

Source: vignettes/gwrs-selection.Rmd
gwrs-selection.Rmd

gwr_select() accepts a response and candidate predictor scope, then compares ordinary Gaussian GWR fits across predictor subsets, kernels and bandwidths. Each candidate is unpenalized. The default ranking criterion is AICc; AIC, BIC, GCV and conditional leave-one-out squared error are reported alongside it. The selected GWR is the best eligible candidate under the chosen criterion within the evaluated search space.

A small reproducible demonstration

The following simulated observations have unitless planar coordinates. They illustrate the interface and are not empirical evidence about a real region. Real applications should supply suitable projected coordinates; the package uses Euclidean distance and does not transform coordinates.

set.seed(1401)
dat <- data.frame(east = runif(28), north = runif(28),
                  x1 = rnorm(28), x2 = rnorm(28))
dat$y <- 1 + (1 + dat$east) * dat$x1 + rnorm(28, sd = 0.5)
selection <- gwr_select(y ~ x1 + x2, dat, c("east", "north"),
  kernels = c("bisquare", "gaussian"), k = c(20, 28),
  control = gwrs_control(n_threads = 1), verbose = FALSE)
selection
#> Joint unpenalized GWR selection
#>   search:exhaustive / complete
#>   evaluated: 16   criterion: aicc 
#>   best GWR: x1 
#>   kernel: gaussian   bandwidth: adaptive 28 
#>   criterion: 39.99189 
#>   Moran: not_calculated: weights_not_supplied 
#>   local coefficient inference: calculated 
#>   flags: grid_boundary 
#>   best including OLS: OLS - x1
knitr::kable(selection$best_by_criterion[, c("criterion", "comparison",
  "terms", "kernel", "k", "criterion_value")], digits = 3)
criterion comparison terms kernel k criterion_value
6 aic GWR x1 gaussian 28 38.780
61 aic overall x1 gaussian 28 38.780
62 aicc GWR x1 gaussian 28 39.992
2 aicc overall x1 NA NA 39.860
63 bic GWR x1 gaussian 28 43.204
21 bic overall x1 NA NA 42.857
64 gcv GWR x1 gaussian 28 0.219
65 gcv overall x1 gaussian 28 0.219
66 loo_cv GWR x1 gaussian 28 6.192
22 loo_cv overall x1 NA NA 6.186

best_model is a fitted GWR object supporting coef() and predict(); best_overall also allows OLS to win. The corresponding metadata are selected and selected_overall. ranking retains every evaluated candidate, including failed or invalid fits and their reasons. summary(selection) shows leading candidates and the selected model’s conditional F1/F2/F3 diagnostics.

Local coefficient p-values and BH adjustment

By default, only the selected GWR is refitted with full diagnostics. Candidate search fits retain standard diagnostics, so local inference is not repeated for every subset/kernel/bandwidth combination. The table below contains two-sided coefficient-zero reference p-values and BH-adjusted p-values. These differ from F3, which concerns spatial constancy of a whole surface.

local <- selection$local_inference
local$status
#> [1] "calculated"
display <- head(local$local[, c("location", "coefficient", "estimate",
  "standard_error", "statistic", "p_value", "p_adjusted")])
display$p_value <- format.pval(display$p_value, digits = 3)
display$p_adjusted <- format.pval(display$p_adjusted, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(display, digits = 4)
location coefficient estimate standard_error statistic p_value p_adjusted
1 (Intercept) 1.0735 0.0861 12.4712 2.50e-12 3.28e-12
2 (Intercept) 1.0875 0.0861 12.6253 1.91e-12 3.28e-12
3 (Intercept) 1.0905 0.0860 12.6745 1.76e-12 3.28e-12
4 (Intercept) 1.0750 0.0859 12.5079 2.35e-12 3.28e-12
5 (Intercept) 1.0587 0.0859 12.3274 3.23e-12 3.28e-12
6 (Intercept) 1.0590 0.0859 12.3344 3.19e-12 3.28e-12 
local$settings[c("adjust", "adjust_scope", "exploratory",
                 "reference_calibrated", "selection_conditioned")]
#> $adjust
#> [1] "BH"
#> 
#> $adjust_scope
#> [1] "coefficient"
#> 
#> $exploratory
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $reference_calibrated
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $selection_conditioned
#> [1] TRUE

P-values are formatted for display; local$local retains the numeric values.

The default BH family is the locations for each design-matrix coefficient separately, including the intercept. Factor contrasts are separate coefficients. To adjust over every local coefficient test in the selected model instead, call the same inference function with an explicit scope:

all_local_tests <- gwr_local_inference(selection, adjust = "BH",
                                       adjust_scope = "global")
all_local_tests$summary
#>   coefficient selected_percent significant_percent median_abs_statistic
#> 1 (Intercept)              100                 100             12.40802
#> 2          x1              100                 100             15.30688
#>   min_adjusted_p available_tests unavailable_tests
#> 1   3.170602e-12              28                 0
#> 2   6.681090e-14              28                 0

All local p-values are exploratory. Neither BH scope accounts for the response-based selection of predictors, kernel and bandwidth; BH does not establish calibration of the underlying reference p-values or remove smoothing bias and dependence between overlapping neighborhoods. No post-selection or calibrated FDR guarantee is claimed. Local p-values never affect model ranking. The selected model and whether the search completed are retained in local$settings$selection.

Set local_inference = FALSE in gwr_select() to skip full diagnostics and local inference; the result records local_inference_status = "disabled". No eligible GWR gives NULL inference with an explicit status. Incomplete searches identify their inference as provisional. Unavailable reference degrees of freedom or coefficient statistics produce NA p-values and significance flags; the function does not silently switch to a normal approximation. df = "normal" is an explicit option for standalone inference.

Define and inspect the search

Factors and multi-column formula terms are selected as whole groups. Interactions require their main effects in the full scope and retain all declared lower-order parents. required accepts term labels or a one-sided formula. Required terms also constrain the OLS comparison; intercept-only OLS is compared only when no terms are required. Intercept-only GWR is not fitted.

All candidates use the same full-scope observations and design coding. Missing or nonfinite values cause an error, with no silent sample deletion or imputation. Standardization defaults to FALSE; setting it to TRUE is an explicit preprocessing choice passed to the existing fitting function.

design <- gwr_select(y ~ x1 + x2, dat, c("east", "north"), dry_run = TRUE)
design
#> GWR selection design (no fits)
#>   n: 28   scope terms: 2 
#>   search: exhaustive   candidates: 389 
#>   neighbor workspace estimate (MiB): 0.01196289 
#>   Moran: not_calculated: weights_not_supplied

The default exhaustive search considers every nonempty hierarchy-valid subset and all five kernels. With adaptive bandwidth and no k, each subset searches all integers from its expanded predictor count plus two through the sample size. k includes the target observation. Adaptive Gaussian and exponential fits retain only these k neighbors, matching the existing package semantics.

For fixed-distance selection, set bandwidth = "fixed" and provide bw in coordinate units. All observations are retained in the neighbor representation; compact kernels assign zero weight outside their radius. Without bw, a 30-value logarithmic grid spans the smallest positive pairwise distance to twice the largest. A finite grid gives no continuous-bandwidth guarantee. Both modes can be requested with bandwidth = c("adaptive", "fixed").

max_models rejects oversized exhaustive designs before fitting. For a larger scope, explicitly choose search = "stepwise": full-model and required-plus-single-term seeds are followed by best-improvement additions and deletions. Each visited subset searches the complete requested kernel/bandwidth grid. This deterministic search has no global-optimum guarantee.

Diagnostics and scientific limits

Eligibility requires full local predictor rank, direct converged solves, finite fitted quantities and positive residual effective degrees of freedom. Each ranking criterion separately requires a finite score. Low effective sample size, high leverage, collinearity and grid-boundary solutions are reported as descriptive flags. Diagnostic p-values do not affect ranking.

F3 tests spatial variability of coefficients, not whether they are zero. F reference distributions are moment-matched approximations. All F and Moran p-values are raw, conditional and exploratory; selection and multiplicity have not been adjusted for. Conditional LOO holds the fitted neighborhoods and weights fixed. It does not replace external or nested spatial validation that repeats model selection inside training folds.

For a fixed smoother, F1 and F2 are decreasing affine transformations of the same residual-sum-of-squares ratio. Their separate moment-matched reference distributions may give different p-values. These are not two independent pieces of evidence, and exact operator moments do not establish calibration of either reference distribution. F3 likewise has no established calibration under response-based selection or spatially varying nuisance coefficients.

Moran is reported as not_calculated: weights_not_supplied by default. To compute it, supply a scientifically chosen common matrix as moran_weights. Rows and columns must follow data order; supplied names must match exactly. Weights must be finite, nonnegative and have zero diagonal. Row standardization is controlled explicitly. Islands fail by default; moran_zero_policy = "keep" retains them in global centering/permutations and marks their local statistics unavailable. No neighbor graph is chosen for you.

Bounded execution and verified resume

A work unit is one candidate fit and its requested diagnostics. The following template uses your already prepared dat and a new versioned output directory. It is not executed when building this guide.

run_dir <- "results/gwr-selection-v01"
partial <- gwr_select(y ~ x1 + x2, dat, c("east", "north"),
  k = c(20, 28), checkpoint = run_dir, max_evaluations = 10,
  control = gwrs_control(n_threads = 1))
gwr_select_verify(run_dir)
finished <- gwr_select(y ~ x1 + x2, dat, c("east", "north"),
  k = c(20, 28), checkpoint = run_dir, resume = TRUE,
  control = gwrs_control(n_threads = 1))
gwr_select_verify(run_dir)

Invocation limits produce explicitly provisional results. Resume verifies data, settings (including Moran seeds/weights and thread controls), software, file sizes and SHA-256 hashes before reusing immutable candidate packs. Uncommitted orphan packs are retained but ignored. A single owned lock prevents concurrent writers. Stale locks are never silently removed: confirm the owner is no longer running, then archive its run.lock directory before resuming.

progress.json and append-only progress.tsv distinguish calculated and durable counts. Search ETA uses measured throughput for new candidates in the current invocation and excludes final refits/output verification; stepwise total work and ETA remain unknown. Progress updates occur between candidates, at most every 30 seconds, so a long individual fit may delay the next heartbeat. Final result and ranking snapshots are numbered without overwriting earlier snapshots. Use gwr_select_verify() for integrity and completeness checks; progress alone is not validation. memory_limit_mb guards estimated neighbor and diagnostic workspaces, not total process memory.
